---
title: A University of Inland Norway Typst template for Quarto
typst-logo:
  path: "logo-eng.png"
course: "Course code"
course-link: "https://www.inn.no"
page-numbering: "none"  # Options: "1", "I", "i", "a", "A", or "none" to disable
margin-notes:
  - title: "Tutor"
    position: 20
    content: "[Professor Adams](mailto:prof.adams@inn.no)"
  - title: "A definition"
    position: 10
    content: "Some text that is defining a concept"
  - title: "Reference"
    position: 15
    content: "See Smith (2023) for further reading."
format:
  innHandout-typst: default
bibliography: bibliography.bib
bibliographystyle: "apa"
reference-section-title: false     # disables Quarto's automatic bibliography heading
bibliography-heading: "References" # our own heading for the bibliography
crossref:
  fig-title: Figure    # (default is "Figure")
  tbl-title: Table     # (default is "Table")
  title-delim: ":"     # (default is ":")
---

## Introduction

This is a simple Quarto/Typst template to match styles of the University of
Inland Norway. This template file contains instructions on how to use the
extension.

Typst is an [open source typesetting system](https://typst.app) used by
[Quarto](https://quarto.org/), an open-source publishing system to render PDFs
from markdown-based source files. Quarto lets you combine prose, data and
computer code to write technical documents.

## Fonts

Aptos, the Microsoft font recommended by INN, may not be available to Typst when
it builds a PDF. To check if you have the font installed, open a terminal and
type:

```bash
quarto typst fonts
```

If you do not find Aptos, Aptos Display, Aptos Mono etc., download the font from
[Microsoft](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/download/details.aspx?id=106087),
select all `.ttf` files, right-click and select Install. Check again
(`quarto typst fonts`) that the fonts are installed.

## Logotypes

There are two main alternatives for logotypes in the upper right corner,
`logo-eng.png` and `logo-nor.png`. These are included in the extension folder.
Change the file name to switch between the English and Norwegian logotype.

## Margin notes and course name

Margin notes can be specified in the YAML field and will display on the first
page of a multipage document. These can include links and other simple markdown
formatting.

The course name (and web address) has a fixed position as part of the footer.
Use the YAML field to modify the content of this key.

Additional margin notes have not been implemented.

## Citations

Citations should work [@teigen2013]. The built-in system for references defaults
to "ieee" but can be changed using the `bibliographystyle` option in the YAML
field. See [here for more
information](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/typst.html#bibliography).
The bibliography heading has been made user-defined using the
`bibliography-heading` key in YAML.

## Tables and figures created with R

Figures from data can be included, and we can cross-reference them. To change
the title of the cross reference, adjust under `crossref` in the YAML field. See
@fig-inn for an example of R-created output.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-inn
#| fig-cap: "This is a figure created with R"

library(tidyverse)

ToothGrowth |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(dose), len, colour = supp)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1)) +
  labs(x = "Dose (mg/day)", y = "Odontoblast length", colour = "Supplement")
```

We can also include figures like @fig-sample in our documents.

![This is a sample caption for the figure. National Library of Norway, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons](faaberg.jpg){#fig-sample}

Tables can also be created from data using R, see @tbl-example.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-example
#| tbl-cap: "This is a table created with R"

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

ToothGrowth |>
  summarise(.by = c(supp, dose),
            Mean = mean(len),
            SD = sd(len)) |>
  arrange(supp, dose) |>
  gt() |>
  # gt's default font stack ends in the CSS keyword `sans-serif`, which Quarto
  # passes through to Typst as a font name; Typst 0.15 (Quarto 1.10) warns
  # about it. Naming the document font here also keeps the table in Aptos.
  tab_options(table.font.names = c("Aptos", "Segoe UI", "Calibri"))
```
